ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
Partner with product owners, product managers, business stakeholders, and SMEs to elicit, analyze, validate, and document functional and non-functional needs, business rules, product requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Translate product objectives and business needs into clear, actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, supporting documentation, and technical specifications that are ready for Agile delivery teams.
Analyze complex business and technical issues, existing system logic, dependencies, and opportunities to improve product outcomes, operational performance, and member or stakeholder experience.
Support product teams in defining scope, sequencing work, and clarifying requirements based on user needs, business value, system dependencies, existing architecture, and enterprise technology direction.
Conduct impact analysis and assessments for proposed product changes to evaluate system dependencies, risks, effort estimates, and traceability needs that inform prioritization, backlog refinement, and delivery planning.
Map business data elements to backend data sources, using SQL skills for accurate querying, validation, and source-to-target mapping.
Create and maintain lightweight, fit-for-purpose documentation that supports product decisions, Agile delivery, system understanding, and downstream development or testing activities; review and provide feedback on vendor designs and deliverables.
Act as a liaison between product, business, engineering, architecture, and QA teams to clarify requirements, resolve questions, support backlog refinement, and ensure a shared understanding of business value, technical scope, and acceptance criteria.
Support Agile delivery teams throughout discovery, sprint planning, development, testing, defect triage, user acceptance testing (UAT), release readiness, and post-release validation activities.
Ensure product requirements, backlog items, and delivery artifacts adhere to BCBSRI policies, standards, and regulatory/compliance requirements (e.g., HIPAA, CMS, BCBSA).
Perform other duties as assigned.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or related field; or an equivalent combination of education and related work experience.
Three to five years of business analysis, systems analysis, or product delivery experience, working with business and product teams to define, refine, and document requirements for technology solutions
Preferred Education, Additional Qualifications and Experience:
Healthcare payer or health insurance industry experience.
Experience with Facets or other healthcare payer adjudication systems.
Experience with cloud-based platform integrations (Azure, Google Cloud, and Salesforce).
Experience supporting Agile product delivery, including backlog refinement, user story development, acceptance criteria, sprint planning, and collaboration with product owners and cross-functional delivery teams.
CCBA, CBAP, or PMI-PBA certification, or familiarity with BABOK / IIBA standards.
Familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to healthcare (HIPAA, CMS, BCBSA, SOC1/SOC2)
Required Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities:
Ability to elicit, analyze, and document business, user, and product requirements, including process flows, user stories, use cases, acceptance criteria, and conceptual data diagrams.
Strong hands-on SQL skills for data mapping, querying, and validation across systems.
Knowledge of requirements engineering, traceability matrices, and requirements management tools and techniques.
Understanding of Agile delivery practices, software development lifecycles (SDLC), API and batch integration concepts, and modern web-based/client-server application design.
Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience creating and validating Agile delivery artifacts and documentation for downstream teams, including developers, QA, deployment, operations, and product stakeholders.
Proficiency with business process modeling and diagramming tools (e.g., Microsoft Visio) and the Microsoft Office suite.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with strong business acumen and political savvy.
Strong written and verbal communication, facilitation, and negotiation skills.
Ability to work effectively with a wide variety of people in individual and group settings.
Strong organizing and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize and respond to shifting deadlines and manage a diverse, deadline-oriented workflow.

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.
We are seeking a QA/DevOps Engineer to join Discord’s Business Systems team. In this role, you will own automated test suite development and maintenance across Oracle ERP Cloud (Fusion) and Salesforce, with a focus on Tosca-based regression and progression testing. You will embed automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and partner closely with ERP Functional, Technical, and DevOps teams to ensure every release is tested consistently and defects are caught early.
What you'll be doing
Run Oracle ERP Cloud and Salesforce QA automation suites for all quarterly patch upgrades end-to-end.
Review new Oracle and SFDC release features and recommend improvements to existing testing processes.
Build and improve regression and progression test automation in the Tosca environment for Oracle Fusion and Salesforce.
Create, maintain, and update Tosca scripts to reflect system and process changes across GL, AP, AR, and FAH modules.
Lead feature enhancement reviews as part of quarterly patch assessment cycles and new enhancement projects.
Integrate automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines; trigger regression suites automatically on every release candidate build.
Maintain test infrastructure and environments in collaboration with DevOps and ERP Technical teams.
Document test coverage, defect trends, and release readiness in Jira and shared reporting dashboards.
Automation Use Cases
FAH Process Automation: Auto-test Financial Accounting Hub on each new sales item addition to eliminate manual unit testing.
AR Regression Suite: Automated flows for invoicing, receipts, and customer setup across every release.
AP Regression Suite: Payment runs, supplier invoices, holds, and approvals tested automatically on each patch cycle.
Salesforce Tosca Automation: Develop, maintain, and expand automated SFDC test suites in Tosca, integrated with release pipelines.
What you should have
3-5+ years of QA automation experience.
Hands-on Tosca experience for regression and progression test suite development and maintenance.
Experience executing and maintaining automated test cycles for quarterly Oracle patch upgrades.
Familiarity with Oracle ERP Cloud and SFDC release feature review and technical impact assessment.
Experience integrating automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or equivalent).
Familiarity with pipeline configuration: triggering regression runs on pull requests and release candidate builds.
Working knowledge of version control (Git / GitHub or GitLab): branching, pull requests, and code review workflows.
Basic scripting capability in Python, Shell, or PowerShell for test utility automation and pipeline support.
Understanding of containerized test environments (Docker); experience running tests in ephemeral containers is a plus.
Jira for defect tracking, test coverage reporting, and sprint participation.
Experience writing and maintaining test documentation: test plans, test cases, regression logs, and release readiness summaries.
Ability to work cross-functionally with ERP Functional Analysts, ERP Technical Developers, and DevOps engineers.
Familiarity with SOX compliance, ITGC controls, and ERP change management practices.
Preferred Qualifications
Oracle Fusion certification or formal training in Oracle ERP Cloud modules.
Experience with SaaS QA automation in a high-growth technology company environment.
Exposure to OIC (Oracle Integration Cloud) or MuleSoft integration testing.
Familiarity with Salesforce test automation frameworks beyond Tosca (Selenium, Provar, or equivalent).
Prior experience working with AMS or managed services vendors in an ERP context.
Knowledge of Oracle quarterly release cycles and technical impact assessments.
Exposure to infrastructure-as-code or environment provisioning concepts (Terraform, Ansible).

About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.
About the Query Team
Every pipeline, job, and test that runs on CircleCI generates data, and that history is one of our biggest advantages in an agentic software delivery lifecycle. Flaky test detection, test insights, pipeline search, and agents that reason about why a build failed all depend on fast, reliable access to it.
The Query team owns the system that makes this possible. We pull product data out of the transactional services that create it and store it in datastores built for historical and analytical workloads. We serve it through domain-level APIs to CircleCI's product teams and to customers through our public API. Our goal is to make storing data "fire and forget" for every other team, and querying it fast and dependable at a scale that keeps growing.
What You'll Do
Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
Shape how we store data at scale. Own and harden our ClickHouse-based storage layer. Design schemas for known and emerging access patterns, and tune ingestion and query performance to support production-scale data.
Build the pipelines that move our data. Design and own ingestion from event streams and durable workflows built on Temporal. Data should arrive reliably, stay queryable while it's in transit, and never slow down the critical path of the services that produce it.
Serve data to the product and to customers. Evolve our platform into the default path for historical queries. Make getting historical data easy, not a bottleneck. Teams should be able to get what they need quickly and with minimal hand-holding, while Query keeps enough visibility into how the data is used to optimize ingestion and reads across every consumer. Build in the indexing, caching, and tiered storage required to keep it performant.
Set technical direction. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you lead the design discussion, write up the architecture decision, and make the call. You help decide which data domain we migrate next and how.
Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand ingestion lag, query latency, and data correctness. For a data platform, operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
Keep things moving. You take ambiguous data problems from design to production quickly, and you help the people around you move faster too.
You don't just patch problems, you ask why they happened. You'll fix the immediate issue, then solve the underlying team practice, process, or system that let it through.
What You'll Bring
AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
Hands-on data experience. You've built or owned data-intensive systems such as ingestion pipelines, event-driven architectures, or analytical and time-series datastores. You understand the tradeoffs between transactional and analytical storage, and you've designed schemas and tuned queries for high-volume workloads. Experience with ClickHouse or another columnar database is a strong plus.
Backend depth in Go. You're strong in Go, or strong in a comparable language and eager to work in Go: interface design, data modeling, service integration, and concurrency. Familiarity with React and TypeScript is a plus, since you'll occasionally work on the product surfaces that display this data.
Distributed systems judgment. You understand delivery guarantees, idempotency, backpressure, and failure recovery. You know when to rely on a framework's reliability guarantees rather than building your own.
Technical leadership. You've led the design of complex systems and made tradeoffs deliberately. You leave foundations others can build on. You raise the quality bar through reviews, mentoring, and direct feedback, not just through the code you write.
A track record of shipping. 5+ years building and operating production backend systems. Your work has served real users, and you've treated latency, reliability, and correctness as design concerns.
Sound like you?
You care about how data powers the product, not just where it lives. You know how to make a datastore fast at scale, and have tuned schemas and queries against real production load. You think like a platform engineer, measuring your work by how much it unblocks the teams building on it. AI isn't a tool you reach for occasionally; it's a core part of how you approach and solve problems. If that sounds like you, we want to talk.
